title: Part 3: berpendapat, membandingkan, berspekulasi
goal: Menjawab pertanyaan abstrak tentang masyarakat dengan posisi yang jelas, alasan yang dikembangkan, dan bahasa spekulasi serta perbandingan yang tepat — termasuk saat kamu tidak punya pendapat sama sekali.
bekal: membangun jawaban 40–60 detik dengan pola posisi, alasan, contoh, sisi lain
memakai modal spekulasi dan conditional tanpa berpikir lama
mengulur waktu dan meminta pengulangan tanpa kehilangan nilai

blocks.text: Empat sampai lima menit terakhir Speaking adalah diskusi. Pemeriksa mengambil tema cue card Part 2 dan menariknya ke tingkat yang lebih abstrak: dari *seorang guru yang berkesan* menjadi *bagaimana peran guru berubah*, dari *tempat yang menenangkan* menjadi *apakah kota bisa dibuat lebih layak huni*. Pertanyaannya lebih panjang, lebih terbuka, dan hampir selalu memuat salah satu penanda ini: *people in your country*, *nowadays*, *in the future*, *do you think*, *why do you think*, *what's the difference between*.

Penanda itu memberitahu satu hal penting: pemeriksa tidak lagi bertanya tentang hidupmu. Jawaban yang kembali ke pengalaman pribadi (*In my family, we always…*) terdengar seperti Part 1 dan menahan nilai. Pengalaman pribadi boleh masuk, tapi sebagai **contoh** dari pernyataan umum, bukan sebagai isi jawaban.

blocks.title: Perbedaan yang harus terasa di telingamu
items: **Part 1:** *Do you like reading?* → tentang kamu, 2–3 kalimat, 15–25 detik.
**Part 3:** *Do you think people read less than they used to?* → tentang masyarakat, 4–6 kalimat, 40–60 detik, dengan alasan yang dikembangkan.

**Yang dinilai berubah bobotnya.** Fluency & Coherence sekarang berarti *mempertahankan argumen*, dan Lexical Resource berarti *bahasa abstrak*: kecenderungan, dampak, kebijakan, generasi. Grammar diuji lewat conditional dan modal, yang hampir tidak muncul di Part 1.

**Tidak ada jawaban yang benar.** Pemeriksa tidak menilai pendapatmu, tidak peduli kamu setuju atau tidak, dan tidak tahu apa-apa tentang topiknya lebih dari kamu. Yang dinilai hanya bagaimana kamu menyusunnya dalam bahasa Inggris.

blocks.text: Sama seperti dua unit sebelumnya: latihan di sini minta kamu merekam diri sendiri. Rekaman berwaktu dengan penilaian AI per kriteria ada di menu **Simulasi** di dashboard.

sections.title: Struktur jawaban: posisi, alasan, contoh, sisi lain

blocks.text: Empat puluh sampai enam puluh detik terdengar lama sampai kamu punya polanya. Pola di bawah ini bekerja untuk hampir semua pertanyaan Part 3 dan bisa dipakai berulang tanpa terdengar mekanis, karena isinya berubah tiap kali.

blocks.title: Empat langkah
items: **1. POSISI (satu kalimat).** Ambil sikap yang jelas, walaupun lunak. *Not entirely, no.* *Some, definitely — though less than people expect.* *I'd say governments carry most of it.* Hindari membuka dengan *It depends*: itu menunda posisimu dan sering berakhir tanpa posisi sama sekali.
**2. ALASAN (satu sampai dua kalimat).** *because*, *simply because of*, *the main reason is*. Satu alasan yang dijelaskan jauh lebih baik daripada tiga alasan yang didaftar.

**3. CONTOH (satu sampai dua kalimat).** *Take … for example.* Boleh dari negaramu, pekerjaanmu, atau angka yang kamu karang dengan wajar. Contoh konkretlah yang mengubah jawaban Band 6 menjadi Band 7.

**4. SISI LAIN (opsional, satu kalimat).** *Having said that, …* *Although I'm not sure …* Menyebut kelemahan argumenmu sendiri menunjukkan kendali, bukan keraguan — asal posisimu di langkah 1 tetap berdiri.

blocks.text: Berhenti di detik ke-60 sekitar. Part 3 punya lima sampai delapan pertanyaan; jawaban dua menit memakan jatah pertanyaan lain dan biasanya mulai berputar. Kalau pemeriksa memotongmu, itu tanda waktunya habis, bukan tanda jawabanmu buruk.
Part 3 sebenarnya hanya menuntut lima gerakan bahasa. Kuasai frasa di tabel ini sampai keluar tanpa dipikir, dan setengah pekerjaan Part 3 selesai.

head: Fungsi
Frasa
Contoh
rows: Memberi opini
*I'd say · Personally · It seems to me · If you ask me · To my mind*
*I'd say the biggest change is how quickly rumours travel now.*
Opini yang lebih tegas
*There's no doubt that · I'm convinced · Clearly*
*There's no doubt that housing has become unaffordable for people my age.*
Membandingkan dulu dan sekarang
*used to · these days · back then · a generation ago · nowhere near as … as*
*People used to buy a paper every morning; these days almost nobody under thirty does.*
Berspekulasi tentang masa depan
*will · is likely to · is bound to · might · I imagine · I'd expect*
*I imagine most of that paperwork will be automated within a decade.*
Menyeimbangkan
*Having said that · That said · On the other hand · It depends largely on*
*Having said that, I'm not sure what would replace exams at that scale.*
Memberi contoh
*Take … for example · A good example would be · You only have to look at …*
*You only have to look at what happened to bookshops.*
Mengakui ketidaktahuan dengan elegan
*I've never really thought about it, but … · I'm not an expert, but my guess would be … · I couldn't say for certain, though …*
*I've never really thought about it, but I'd guess it comes down to cost.*
Menolak dengan halus
*I see what you mean, but … · Where I'd push back is … · I'm not sure that's the main reason*
*I see what you mean, but I don't think that's the whole story.*

blocks.text: Baris ketujuh adalah penyelamat terpenting di unit ini. Kamu **akan** mendapat satu pertanyaan yang tidak pernah kamu pikirkan seumur hidup — tentang kebijakan pertanian, museum, atau pendidikan anak usia dini. Diam berarti Fluency turun; mengakui itu dalam bahasa Inggris yang rapi lalu tetap memberi tebakan justru menaikkannya. *I've never really thought about it, but I'd guess…* adalah kalimat Band 7, bukan pengakuan kalah.

sections.title: Tiga struktur grammar yang paling terasa di Part 3

blocks.text: Grammatical Range dinilai dari **variasi**, dan Part 3 adalah satu-satunya tempat di mana tiga struktur ini muncul alami. Pakai masing-masing sekali atau dua kali; lebih dari itu terdengar dipaksakan.

head: Conditional
Dipakai untuk
Contoh Part 3
rows: *If* + present, *will*
Prediksi yang realistis
*If universities keep raising fees, fewer people will apply.*
*If* + past, *would*
Situasi hipotetis — struktur paling berguna di Part 3
*If people worked four days a week, cities would be a great deal quieter.*
*If* + past perfect, *would have*
Menilai keputusan masa lalu
*If the government had invested in rail twenty years ago, we wouldn't have this problem.*
*Unless · as long as · provided that*
Syarat, tanpa kata *if*
*Unless it's made cheaper, most families simply won't switch.*

head: Perbandingan
Contoh
Kenapa berguna
rows: *far · much · considerably* + comparative
*Housing is far more expensive than it was ten years ago.*
Menguatkan perbandingan tanpa mengulang *very*
*nowhere near as … as*
*Public transport is nowhere near as reliable as people assume.*
Perbandingan negatif yang halus
*the more …, the more …*
*The more people move into the city, the worse the traffic gets.*
Struktur yang langsung terdengar Band 7 ke atas
*twice as many · a third of · half the number*
*Twice as many people work from home as did in 2019.*
Perbandingan berangka, terdengar terinformasi
*whereas · while · compared with*
*Older people still read newspapers, whereas my generation gets everything from a phone.*
Kontras dua kelompok dalam satu kalimat

head: Derajat keyakinan
Frasa
Contoh
rows: Hampir pasti
*will · is bound to*
*Prices are bound to keep rising.*
Sangat mungkin
*is likely to · I'd expect*
*Remote work is likely to become the norm for office jobs.*
Mungkin
*might · may · could · possibly*
*Some smaller universities might disappear altogether.*
Dugaan pribadi
*I suspect · I imagine · my guess would be*
*I suspect it'll be a lot slower than people think.*
Tidak mungkin
*is unlikely to · I doubt*
*I doubt printed books will disappear completely.*

blocks.text: Satu jebakan pada baris kedua tabel perbandingan: pilih *is nowhere near as reliable as* ATAU *isn't nearly as reliable as* — jangan digabung menjadi *isn't nowhere near*, karena itu negatif ganda. Kesalahan semacam ini justru muncul saat seseorang mencoba struktur yang lebih tinggi, dan pemeriksa memaafkannya jauh lebih mudah daripada kalimat sederhana yang salah.

sections.title: Mengulur waktu, minta ulang, dan lima belas pertanyaan latihan

blocks.title: Dua detik untuk berpikir, dengan sopan
items: *Hmm, let me think about that for a second.* — paling aman, pakai sekali atau dua kali saja.
*That's an interesting question, actually.* — sekali. Kalau dipakai tiap pertanyaan, terdengar seperti tombol yang ditekan.
*I suppose it depends on what you mean by "successful".* — dua manfaat sekaligus: mengulur waktu DAN mempersempit pertanyaan menjadi sesuatu yang bisa kamu jawab.
*Well, there are a couple of ways of looking at that.* — sekaligus menjanjikan struktur, jadi pastikan kamu benar-benar memberi dua sudut.
Yang harus dihindari: mengulang pertanyaan pemeriksa kata demi kata. Itu terdengar jelas sebagai pengisi waktu dan tidak menambah satu pun kata yang dinilai.

blocks.title: Kalau kamu tidak menangkap pertanyaannya
items: *Sorry, could you repeat that?* atau *Would you mind saying that again?* — pemeriksa boleh mengulang, dan meminta ulang SEKALI tidak menurunkan nilai apa pun.
*Do you mean … or …?* — menebak arah pertanyaan sambil meminta konfirmasi. Ini justru terdengar canggih.

Pemeriksa biasanya mengulang dengan kata yang **sama**, bukan memparafrase. Jadi kalau ada satu kata yang tidak kamu kenal, tebak dari sisa kalimatnya dan jawab arah umumnya — itu jauh lebih baik daripada meminta ulang tiga kali.
Yang benar-benar merugikan adalah menjawab pertanyaan LAIN karena malu bertanya. Pemeriksa akan menilai jawabanmu sebagai tidak relevan, dan itu memukul Fluency & Coherence.

head: Topik
Tiga pertanyaan yang khas
rows: Pendidikan
Do you think exams are a fair way to measure ability? · How has the role of teachers changed over the last thirty years? · Should governments spend more on primary schools or on universities?
Teknologi
In what ways has technology changed the way people communicate? · Do you think artificial intelligence will replace many jobs? · Are older people at a disadvantage in a digital society?
Lingkungan

Whose responsibility is it to protect the environment, individuals or governments? · Why do people find it hard to change their habits, even when they know the risks? · Do you think cities will become greener in the future?
Kota
What are the main problems of living in a large city? · Why do young people keep moving to cities despite the cost? · How could city centres be made more pleasant to live in?
Media
How do people in your country get their news these days? · Do you think news reporting is less trustworthy than it used to be? · Should there be limits on what social media companies publish?

blocks.text: Kerjakan lima belas pertanyaan ini berturut-turut dengan timer 60 detik per pertanyaan, tanpa jeda di antaranya. Itu kira-kira tiga kali beban Part 3 yang sebenarnya — dan setelah latihan seperti itu, lima menit di ruang ujian terasa pendek.

sections.title: Tiga contoh dibedah, dan tugas rekam

blocks.text: Contoh 1 — *Do you think exams are a fair way to measure ability?*

blocks.title: Band 6 lalu Band 7.5
items: **Band 6:** *I think exams are not really fair, because some students are nervous and they cannot show their real ability. But exams are also necessary because we need to know the level of the students. So it depends.*

**Band 7.5:** *Not entirely, no. They measure one thing quite well — how much you can recall under pressure — and that is a real skill, but it's a narrow one. Someone who's brilliant in a lab, or in front of a class, can still freeze in a three-hour paper. Having said that, I'm not sure what would replace them at scale. Coursework is fairer in principle, but it's far easier to buy, and with millions of students you need something you can mark consistently. So I'd keep exams, but I'd make them count for less.*

blocks.text: Contoh 2 — *Do you think artificial intelligence will replace many jobs?*

blocks.title: Band 6 lalu Band 7.5
items: **Band 6:** *Yes, I think AI will replace many jobs in the future. For example factory workers and drivers. But it will also create new jobs, so it is both good and bad.*

**Band 7.5:** *Some, definitely — though I suspect it'll be less dramatic than people expect. What's likely to happen is that it takes over parts of a job rather than the whole thing. A radiologist still reads the scan; the software just flags what to look at first. The jobs most at risk are probably the ones that are mostly routine paperwork, and honestly those have been disappearing for decades anyway. What worries me more is the speed. If the change took thirty years, people would retrain. If it takes five, a lot of people get left behind, and that's a political problem more than a technological one.*

blocks.text: Contoh 3 — *Whose responsibility is it to protect the environment, individuals or governments?*

blocks.title: Band 6 lalu Band 7.5
items: **Band 6:** *I think both of them are responsible. Individuals should recycle and save water, and governments should make laws. If everyone does their part, the environment will be better.*

**Band 7.5:** *I've never really thought about it in those terms, but I'd say governments carry most of it, simply because of scale. If I stop using plastic bags, that's a few hundred bags a year. If a government bans them, that's billions. That said, governments only move when they think voters care, so individual behaviour matters indirectly — it's what makes the policy possible in the first place. Where I'd push back is the idea that it's all personal choice. That framing has been rather convenient for the industries doing the most damage.*

head: Kriteria
Yang dilakukan jawaban Band 6
Yang dilakukan jawaban Band 7.5
rows: Fluency & Coherence
Tiga kalimat lalu berhenti di *so it depends* — posisi batal, argumen tidak dikembangkan.
Empat sampai enam kalimat yang saling membangun; posisi diambil di kalimat pertama dan masih berdiri di kalimat terakhir.
Pengembangan
Alasan didaftar tanpa contoh: *some students are nervous*.
Tiap alasan diikuti contoh konkret: *a radiologist still reads the scan*, *a few hundred bags versus billions*.
Lexical Resource
*good, bad, important, necessary, do their part* — kosakata umum yang bisa dipakai untuk topik apa pun.
*recall under pressure, at scale, mark consistently, routine paperwork, get left behind, that framing* — kosakata yang hanya cocok untuk topik ini.
Grammatical Range
Present simple dan satu first conditional. Tidak ada modal spekulasi.

*I suspect it'll be*, *What's likely to happen is that*, second conditional (*If the change took thirty years, people would retrain*), kontras *If … takes five*, dan present perfect (*have been disappearing*).
Sikap
Menghindari posisi (*it is both good and bad*).
Mengambil posisi lalu MENGUJI posisinya sendiri (*Having said that*, *That said*, *Where I'd push back is*) — inilah yang dibaca deskriptor sebagai diskusi, bukan daftar.

blocks.title: Untuk Latihan 4 — daftar fungsi
items: **A** — memberi opini
**B** — membandingkan dulu dan sekarang
**C** — berspekulasi tentang masa depan
**D** — menyeimbangkan argumen
**E** — mengakui ketidaktahuan dengan elegan

blocks.title: Tugas rekam (5 menit, timer 60 detik per pertanyaan)
items: 1. *Why do young people keep moving to big cities, even when the cost of living there is so high?*
2. *Do you think news reporting is less trustworthy than it used to be?*
3. *If people worked four days a week instead of five, what would change in your country?*

Rekam ketiganya berturut-turut. Lalu dengarkan sambil memeriksa: apakah posisimu sudah jelas di kalimat pertama, apakah ada satu contoh konkret, apakah ada satu conditional, dan apakah kamu bertahan sampai 45 detik. Model untuk pertanyaan 1 dan 2 ada di *Pembahasan*.

exercises.prompt: Which answer is better developed for Part 3? Write A or B. — Artinya: jawaban mana yang lebih berkembang untuk Part 3? Tulis A atau B.
items: *Do you think people read less than they used to?* (A) *Yes, people read less because they use phone too much. It is bad for them.* (B) *Less print, definitely — though I'm not sure they read less overall. My students read constantly; it's just captions and threads rather than books.* ____

*Will electric cars solve air pollution in cities?* (A) *They'd certainly help with the air, though I suspect the traffic itself would stay exactly the same. You still need the same amount of road for the same number of cars.* (B) *Yes, electric cars are very good for the environment because they have no emission, so the pollution will be reduced.* ____

*Should university education be free?* (A) *Yes, it should be free, because education is important for everybody and the government must pay for it.* (B) *Ideally, yes. Although if it's free for everyone, you either raise taxes or you take fewer students — and in most countries that's ended up meaning fewer places, which isn't obviously fairer.* ____

*How has social media changed the news?* (A) *Social media has changed the news very much. Now people can get the news very fast and it is very convenient for them.* (B) *The speed, mainly. A story reaches people before anyone's had time to check it, which is why a correction never catches up with the original.* ____

exercises.prompt: Complete each Part 3 answer with a phrase from the box. — Artinya: lengkapi tiap jawaban Part 3 dengan frasa dari kotak.
pilihan: I've never really thought about it
items: ____ the biggest change is how quickly a rumour can spread now.
Remote work ____ become the norm for most office jobs within ten years.
____, I'm not sure the technology on its own will solve anything.
____, but my guess would be that it comes down to cost more than anything else.

exercises.prompt: Strategi Part 3: TRUE kalau pernyataan itu benar, FALSE kalau tidak.
items: Pertanyaan Part 3 biasanya meminta pendapatmu tentang masyarakat, bukan cerita pribadimu. ____
Meminta pemeriksa mengulang pertanyaan satu kali akan menurunkan nilaimu. ____
Menyebut sisi lain dari argumenmu bisa menaikkan nilai, selama posisimu tetap jelas. ____

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence with its function (A–E) from the list in the last section. — Artinya: cocokkan tiap kalimat dengan fungsinya (A–E) dari daftar di bagian terakhir.
items: *People used to buy a paper every morning; these days almost nobody does.* ____
*Having said that, I'm not sure a ban would actually work in practice.* ____
*I'm not an expert on this, but my guess would be that it's mostly about cost.* ____
*I imagine most of that work will be automated within a decade.* ____

exercises.prompt: Each sentence contains one grammar mistake. Write the correct word only. — Artinya: tiap kalimat memuat satu kesalahan tata bahasa. Tulis kata yang benar saja.
items: *If people would work four days a week, cities would be quieter.* → If people ____ four days a week, cities would be quieter.
*Housing is far more expensive than it was ten years ago, and salaries are not what they was.* → salaries are not what they ____.
*I think education is more important as money.* → I think education is more important ____ money.

answers: I'd say — is likely to — Having said that — I've never really thought about it

head: No
Jawaban
Alasan
rows: B

A memberi satu alasan lalu menilai (*it is bad*) tanpa bukti. B mengambil posisi yang lebih halus (*less print, but not less overall*) dan langsung memberi contoh — persis pola posisi, alasan, contoh.
A
B memakai kalimat yang bisa ditempel di topik lingkungan mana pun. A membedakan dua hal yang berbeda — polusi udara dan kemacetan — dan itulah yang deskriptor sebut *develops the topic*.
B
A hanya menyatakan kewajiban. B menguji gagasannya sendiri dengan konsekuensi (*raise taxes or take fewer students*) dan menutup dengan penilaian, memakai *which isn't obviously fairer*.
B
A mengulang pertanyaan lalu memberi satu kata kunci (*convenient*). B memilih SATU perubahan (*the speed*) dan menjelaskan akibatnya — satu poin yang digali selalu mengalahkan tiga poin yang disebut.
I'd say
Penanda opini yang lebih halus daripada *I think*, dan tidak terdengar diulang-ulang. *Might* tidak cocok karena kalimatnya menyatakan pendapat, bukan kemungkinan.
is likely to
Prediksi yang kuat tapi tidak mutlak. *Might become* juga masuk akal secara makna, tapi kalimat ini menyebut kerangka waktu yang tegas (*within ten years*), yang menuntut keyakinan lebih tinggi.
Having said that
Menandai belokan argumen — kalimat sebelumnya pasti positif tentang teknologi. Ini frasa penyeimbang yang paling sering muncul di jawaban Band 7 ke atas.
I've never really thought about it
Diikuti *but my guess would be…*. Mengakui ketidaktahuan LALU tetap menjawab: cara paling elegan menghadapi pertanyaan asing, dan jauh lebih baik daripada diam empat detik.
FALSE
Meminta ulang sekali tidak menurunkan nilai apa pun. Yang menurunkan nilai adalah menjawab pertanyaan yang berbeda karena malu bertanya.
B — D — E — C
Perhatikan bahwa E (*I'm not an expert, but my guess would be…*) tetap berisi jawaban. Frasa mengaku tidak tahu hanya bernilai kalau dilanjutkan tebakan; kalau berhenti di situ, itu jawaban kosong.
worked
Second conditional: *If* + past simple, lalu *would*. *If people would work* adalah kesalahan yang sangat sering terdengar dan langsung tertangkap telinga pemeriksa.
were
*what they were* — *they* jamak. Kesalahan ini muncul justru saat siswa memakai struktur yang lebih ambisius.
than
Perbandingan memakai *than*, bukan *as*. *As … as* dipakai untuk kesetaraan: *as important as money*.

blocks.title: 1 — *Why do young people keep moving to big cities, even when the cost of living there is so high?*
items: *Work, mainly — but I don't think that's the whole story. The jobs my generation actually wants simply don't exist in smaller towns; there's no design studio in a town of forty thousand people. But there's also the anonymity. In a small town everyone knows whose son you are and what you failed at. In Jakarta nobody knows, and for a lot of people that's worth the rent on its own. Having said that, if remote work really does become normal, I'd expect some of that flow to reverse — not back to the villages, but to mid-sized cities where you can still afford a house.*

blocks.title: 2 — *Do you think news reporting is less trustworthy than it used to be?*
items: *Less trustworthy, or just more visible? I'd say the reporting itself is probably about as good as it ever was — what's changed is that we can now see how it's made. Thirty years ago you got one paper and you believed it, because there was nothing to compare it with. Now the same story reaches you from six directions and the contradictions are obvious. The genuine problem, I think, is speed. Newsrooms are far smaller than they were, and they're expected to publish faster, so the checking gets squeezed. That's a business problem more than an ethical one.*

head: Kriteria
Yang membuat dua model di atas Band 7.5
rows: Posisi

Keduanya mengambil sikap di kalimat pertama, dan model kedua bahkan menantang premis pertanyaannya (*Less trustworthy, or just more visible?*) — gerakan Band 8 yang aman dipakai kalau kamu bisa melanjutkannya.
Pengembangan
Dua alasan yang berbeda JENIS, bukan dua alasan yang mirip: ekonomi dan psikologis di model 1; teknologi dan bisnis di model 2.
Lexical Resource
*the anonymity*, *worth the rent on its own*, *that flow to reverse*, *the contradictions are obvious*, *the checking gets squeezed* — abstrak tapi tetap terdengar seperti bicara.
Grammatical Range

*if remote work really does become normal, I'd expect …* (first conditional dengan penekanan *does*), *about as good as it ever was*, *far smaller than they were*, *they're expected to publish faster* (pasif).
Panjang
Sekitar 50 detik masing-masing. Cukup untuk mengembangkan, tidak cukup untuk mengulang diri sendiri.

blocks.title: Yang perlu dicatat
items: Kalau kamu hanya bisa mengingat satu hal dari unit ini: **ambil posisi di kalimat pertama, lalu beri satu contoh konkret.** Dua gerakan itu saja sudah memisahkan Band 6 dari Band 7 di hampir semua jawaban Part 3.
Kosakata Part 3 tidak perlu akademik. Yang dinilai adalah ketepatan pada topik itu — *routine paperwork*, *at scale*, *the checking gets squeezed* — bukan panjang katanya.

Latih pertanyaan yang tidak kamu pedulikan sama sekali. Topik yang kamu suka membuatmu merasa lancar dan menyembunyikan kelemahannya; pertanyaan tentang museum atau kebijakan pertanian yang menunjukkan apakah pola empat langkahmu benar-benar otomatis.
